newsitem.title: USA: Gore announces steps to improve IRS practices.
newsitem.headline: Gore announces steps to improve IRS practices.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore and Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin Tuesday announced a series of steps to improve the Internal Revenue Service, including creation of a customer service task force.
Americans "deserve to know that their federal government is giving them the most value for their money," Gore said.
"That means creating an IRS that is modern, flexible, and responsive to the needs of its customers -- the American taxpayers," Gore said.
The customer task force will be charged with reviewing problems taxpayers have in dealing with the IRS and propose within 90 days changes to deal with them.
Rubin said the administration also would seek an executive order and legislation to create an IRS oversight board made up of officials.
He said he would issue an order establishing an IRS advisory board made up of individuals outside government who would advise the treasury secretary.
Rubin also said he will propose legislation that will give the IRS commissioner a fixed five-year term to provide "greater continuity of leadership and improved focus."
